body:
This action is a great example of the power of the Lusat action builder.

It's very similar to defining procedures in the beloved [**tRPC**](https://trpc.io), in fact it uses a similar builder syntax, input schema system, and type inference.

By calling `action()` we start a new builder chain. 

We can add a description, compatible with OpenAI Function Calling through the `gptFunctions` adapter, with the `.describe()` builder method. This is the same as the syntax for describing individual parts of the input schema through Zod's own `.describe()` methods.

Then, we define our input schema with Zod and the `.input()` builder method. This will not only register a Zod schema with which Lusat will automatically parse & validate input data when the action is called autonomously by the AI, but also provides the inferred typesafety we need to define our handler without manually writing types. Two birds, one stone.

Finally, the `.handle()` method ends the builder chain, and guarantees that our action handler consumes the type parsed by the input schema, completing our action.

Same process more or less applies to the other functions converted 1-to-1 from @Zakinator123 and @jaredpalmer's manual example.
